bug_locations: The `last` variable was shared across all users instead of being per-user
The sort key only used timestamp, not (user, timestamp), causing interleaving of users
The gap check used a global `last` instead of per-user last timestamp
The condition `if last is not None` was checked globally rather than per-user
explanation: Two main bugs: (1) The `last` variable tracked the last timestamp globally across all users, but it should track the last timestamp per user. This caused incorrect session splitting when multiple users' events were interleaved. (2) The sort key only sorted by timestamp, which could interleave events from different users. Sorting by (user, timestamp) ensures each user's events are processed together. The fix uses a `last` dictionary keyed by user, and checks/updates `last[user]` instead of a global `last`. The `elif` ensures the gap check only happens when the user already has entries (replacing the `if last is not None` guard).
